noise_floor.grid_cap_note: grid.x is capped at 65535 (classic launch bound), so at n > 65535*block = 16777216 the kernel only covers grid*block elements. The n=2^26 cell therefore measures the first 16777216 elements, not 67108864.
noise_floor.crossover_definition: smallest n where (batched scale - batched empty) exceeds 10% of that cell's empty-kernel launch cost; below it, measuring this kernel measures launch overhead

1024.components_measured_in_different_modes: NOT a partition: reported_single is single-mode scale; irreducible_launch and kernel_work are batched-mode differences; measurement_overhead is single-minus-batched. The residual column is what is left over, and it is not small -- do not sum these four as if they decomposed exactly. The kernel_work figure itself is sound: it is the internally consistent batched difference.

noise_floor.mdd_pct_by_n_note:
READ THIS BEFORE USING THE BLOCK ABOVE.
(1) The top-level mdd_pct_by_n is the curve for exactly ONE cell -- empty/single/n=1024, ts job 20260927t162535-cb00ea78 -- and is NOT a bound on this measurement. The worst case among the empty-kernel single-mode cells is n=16384 at 76.3 % for N=10; the top-level 51.4 % is neither that worst case nor a limit on anything.
(2) MDD is NOT monotone in problem size across those cells: n=1024 -> 51.4 %, n=16384 -> 76.3 %, n=262144 -> 27.8 %, n=4194304 -> 11.2 %, n=67108864 -> 2.3 % (all at N=10). It peaks at an intermediate size, so 'smaller is noisier' does not hold.
(3) MDD tracks within-process noise, as it must (it is computed from within-process std and the median): Pearson r(MDD@N=10, within-process cv) = +0.929 over all 20 cells; +0.950 over the 5 empty single-mode cells [SUBSET -- do not quote as a headline]. The across-invocation column tracks about equally well and may also be used: r(MDD@N=10, across-invocation CV) = +0.929 over all 20 cells, measured from cells[].across_invocations_spread_pct. (An earlier correction put this at +0.926; the figure here is the one recomputed from this artifact.)
(4) A cell's median_ms is the MEDIAN OF ITS THREE per-invocation medians, not any single run. Those invocation medians span 27.6-37.7 % in the sub-10 us regime (n=16384: 1.472 / 2.208 / 2.304 us; n=1024: 2.144 / 2.144 / 1.552 us). Every one of those is a real measurement of that cell. So no single-run figure from this regime may be quoted as a cell's runtime, and the three-invocation median is the MINIMUM defensible estimator, not a refinement.
(5) r(median, within-process cv) = -0.414 over all 20 cells: low medians and high cv co-occur, most strongly in the single-mode cells. The sign survives; the MAGNITUDE is not established, and no median here is called systematically biased on this evidence.
Rule applied throughout: every figure names the cell it came from, and every correlation names the population it was computed over.
